title: Holistic warm-orchestration for dedicated fleets: staged weight streaming and JIT KV priming
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Dedicated customers are experiencing variable tail latency and token-level cost spikes when new model variants or tenants are routed to cold workers. Existing warm-pool approaches pre-load weights or keep idle GPUs, but we lack a coordinated orchestration that simultaneously guarantees throughput SLOs, minimizes memory pressure, and primesthe KV cache for common prompt prefixes.
goals: Provide deterministic throughput guarantees for tenant bursts by coordinating weight streaming and KV priming across the warm pool
Reduce percentiles for cold-start latency (P95/P99) to target SLOs defined per capacity tier
Bound additional resource and cost overhead of prewarming (memory, network, I/O) via configurable budgets
Integrate with predictive autoscaler to align prewarming actions to upcoming load while preserving fairness across tenants
success_metrics: P95 cold-start token latency reduced by >= 50% for first 30s after scale-out
Sustained throughput within 90% of provisioned guarantee within 10s of routing a new tenant
Prewarm cost overhead < 8% of baseline GPU hours for steady-state fleet
design_summary: Introduce a two-phase warm orchestration controller: (1) Staged weight streaming: progressively fetch model sharded weights prioritized by execution-critical layers and KV table residency, allowing earliest tokens to be served while remaining weights stream in background; (2) JIT KV priming: use sampled tenant traces + short synthetic probes to populate KV caches with high-likelihood prefixes and KV snapshots. The controller will expose per-tenant priority, budget (GB and network), and a cold-window tolerance that other components (router, autoscaler) can query.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Prefer progressive weight availability over full eager staging to reduce memory pressure at scale — increases implementation complexity but lowers prewarm cost
KV priming uses probabilistic sampling of historical prompts; this risks stale prefixes for rapidly changing apps — mitigated by a short lived TTL and quick re-probing on mispredictions
Admission control will temporarily route low-priority traffic to best-effort workers during simultaneous fleet-wide prewarms to protect throughput guarantees for paid tiers
implementation_plan: Controller: new warm-orch service that maintains warm pool state and prewarm plans (GRPC API) — 2w
Worker runtime changes: accept progressive weight segments and expose priming hooks for KV snapshot ingestion — 3w
Router integration: query warm-orch for destination preferences and honor admission control during high-concurrency scale-outs — 1w
Autoscaler integration: feedback loop to request prewarm ahead of predicted ramp (adapt window and budget) — 1w
Canary + rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag with telemetry and per-tenant toggle — 1w
monitoring_and_alerting: Grafana: warm_pool.health (count healthy prewarmed workers), warm_pool.inflight_streams, priming.success_rate
Alerts: priming_success_rate < 90% over 5m, steady_throughput not reached within cold_window for >10 tenants
rollout_plan: Start with internal dedicated clusters and a single non-critical tenant cohort. Run for two weeks and compare metrics vs. control. If P95 improvement and prewarm costs within budget, expand to all dedicated fleets by region. Provide per-tenant opt-out flag and administrative prewarm budget adjustments in Console.
risks_and_mitigations: Network saturation when many workers stream weights simultaneously — mitigation: global prewarm rate limiter and shard-aware staggered streaming
Incorrect priming causing wasted memory and GPU residency — mitigation: conservative priming budgets + fast eviction policy and continuous sampling feedback
Behavioral regressions with progressive weights (partial execution) — mitigation: heavy unit/e2e test matrix and runtime fallbacks to full load if early-token quality unacceptable
